The maths you already did.

Nothing in this hour is new to you. All of it is your degree.

Everything today is Class 12 mathematics. In four years you will call the same objects by other names: impedance, transfer function, bit error rate.

Ten questions. Answer them honestly, including the ones you get wrong — those are the useful ones.

Your Class 12 syllabus, retitled

Call out a chapter. It already has an electronics name.

Pick one.

Differentiation

A capacitor does not read voltage. It reads the derivative of voltage.

Before I move that slider: bigger capacitor, bigger or smaller current?

i = C · dv/dt

Integration

The plug in this wall says 230 V. No instant of it is ever 230 V.

Vrms = √( (1/T) ∫ v² dt )

peak 1.00 · rms 0.707 · ratio 0.707

A triangle wave peaks at 1 V. What is its rms, to three places?

1/√3 = 0.577. Same integral, different shape, different answer.

Complex numbers

j is not imaginary. j is a 90-degree turn.

current value 1

d/dt (ejωt) = jω · ejωt

Differentiating became multiplying. That single line turns the calculus of circuits into algebra, and it is the reason impedance exists at all.

Differential equations

You solved dy/dx + Py = Q. Here it is, with a soldering iron.

Predict first: I double R and halve C. Does this curve move?

RC · dv/dt + v = Vs

v(t) = Vs(1 − e−t/RC)

τ = 100 ms · 5τ = 500 ms

You need τ = 470 ms with a 10 µF capacitor. What resistance, in kΩ?

47 kΩ. τ = RC, so R = 470 ms / 10 µF = 47 kΩ — and 47 k is a standard value, which is not a coincidence.

Matrices and determinants

Two loops in a circuit is a 2×2 system. Nothing more.

[ 320 −220 ] [i₁] = [10]
[ −220 370 ] [i₂] = [  0]

det 70000 · i₁ 52.9 mA · i₂ 31.4 mA

Vectors

Two 5 volt sources in series. The answer is not ten.

resultant 10.00 V

At what angle is the resultant exactly 5 V?

120°. |V| = 10|cos(φ/2)|, so cos(φ/2) = 0.5 gives φ/2 = 60°. Three sources 120° apart summing to zero is exactly how three-phase power works.

Logarithmsdrop if behind

Why does every number in electronics come with dB after it?

total ×1000 = 30 dB

Doubling the power is how many dB?

10·log₁₀(2) = 3.01 dB. Worth memorising — every 3 dB is a doubling, and you will use it in every lab report for four years.

Sampling

Why wheels spin backwards in films — and why your music is 44,100 Hz.

you perceive 0.30 · direction forward

Probability

Your phone gets bits wrong constantly. It is designed to.

Same slider position, new bits. Predict: same number of errors?

error rate 0.0000 · errors 0 / 400

You are not starting from zero. You are starting from Class 12, and that turns out to be most of the way in.

Three to take home

1. Why is 47 kΩ a standard resistor value and 50 kΩ is not?
2. Your phone charger is rated 5 V. Peak or rms? Why does the answer differ from mains?
3. A hummingbird's wings beat 50 times a second. What frame rate would make them look still?

ACT TWO

Now analyse something.

Act I showed you the tools. Nobody hands you the answer from here.

For the rest of this session you are given a signal that nobody has told you anything about. Your job is to work out what is inside it.

There is no formula on the screen for this. There is a measurement, a way of looking at it, and your judgement.

That gap — between knowing a method and deciding which one to reach for — is the whole of engineering.

Reference cards unlock as you go

Each one summarises what you have just worked out for yourself. Read them after, never before — a summary you have not earned is only something to memorise.

What is a signal?

Not a definition to learn. A test you can apply to anything in this room.

Shout them out. Anything in this room, or on you, that carries information by varying. I will type them in. Target: fifteen in ninety seconds.

counted 0

Analog and digital

Digital is not "better". Digital is an approximation you choose to accept.

Predict before you drag: does the error ever reach zero?

levels 8
largest error 6.2 %
signal-to-noise 19.8 dB

Drag from 1 to 10 bits and watch the dB readout. Work out the rule yourself before answering.

Each extra bit buys you how many dB?

6.02 dB per bit. One more bit halves the step size, and halving an error is 6 dB — the same 3-dB-per-doubling rule from Act I, applied twice. This is why 16-bit audio is quoted at about 96 dB, and why nobody argues about it.

The Signal Detective

Here is a signal. Nobody will tell you what is in it.

Look at it in time. Then look at it in frequency. One of those two views answers the question and the other does not. That choice is the entire skill.

Three tones are hiding in there. Find them, in Hz.

15, 40 and 90 Hz. In the time view they are hopelessly tangled. In the frequency view they are three spikes you can read off with a ruler. Same data, same information — one view made it visible and the other hid it. Choosing the view is not a step in the method; it is the method.

When does a signal disappear?

Not a yes-or-no question. A judgement call, and you have to make it.

15 Hz clear · 40 Hz clear · 90 Hz clear

Turn the noise up slowly. Stop the moment you would no longer stake a lab report on the 90 Hz tone being real. Write your number down before I show the detector's answer.

Filters

Your first design brief. There is more than one right answer.

kept: —

Brief: deliver the 40 Hz tone on its own. Nothing else may survive. Get there, then tell me how much margin you left on each side and why.

Frequencydrop if behind

Every sound you have ever heard was a number.

band audible · who hears it humans, dogs, bats

Slide down below 20 Hz and up past 20 kHz. Everything outside that window is still there. You have simply never had the sensor for it.

You have the tools

Everything you did in the last half hour, you did without being taught it.

You chose a view. You set a threshold and defended it. You made a design trade-off with no single right answer.

Nobody examined you on any of that, and all three are what you will actually be paid for.

Before the next session

Find one signal in your own life. Name what varies, name what you would measure, and name the one thing that would ruin the measurement. Three sentences. That is a complete engineering analysis.
